title: Transport for the Malta trip (13–19 October 2026)
intro: Start with the organizer’s actual attendee location and daily finish time. Route 186 and Route 214 are public-bus candidates between Qawra and Ta’ Qali, not confirmed hotel-to-entrance journeys. Malta Public Transport’s published fares were read directly on 11 October 2026 (single day-route journeys €2.50 in the summer window / €2.00 in winter, €3.00 night and Tallinja Direct, €3.50 on TD1, €19 for 12 journeys, €25 for the 7-day Explore Adult card), and travel cards can be bought at the Buġibba Terminal. Ticket-holder access to the Thunderpick Finals is still unconfirmed; use the date-specific planner for both directions and keep a live-quote taxi fallback, especially for the 17 October evening diversion. Confirmed 11 October 2026: the attendee venue is BLAST Arena Studios Malta, MFCC South Gate National Stadium, ATD 4000 Attard, running 14–18 October with event days listed to 22:00–22:30. That outlasts the last listed bus departure from the Ta’ Qali Stadium area (20:53), so plan a taxi or ride-hailing return, or leave early.

records.name: Qawra ↔ Ta’ Qali Stadium — Route 186 (direct bus to the event area)

TOWARD TA' QALI / RABAT: Buġibba Bay 6 (3531) → Ben (949) → Il-Qawra Arznell (950) → Luzzu (951) → Qawra (952) → Boxxla (953) → Fugass (954) → Wileg (955) → Burmarrad → Mosta (Targa 1138, Rotunda 4 2565, Bezzina 1102, Gholja 1/2) → Ta' Qali Stadium (6227) → Villagg (6228) → Snajja (2191) → Rabat (Rabat 4 2567). RETURN TOWARD BUĠIBBA: Rabat 2 (2569) → Mdina (135) → Saqqajja (4627) → Ta' Qali Stadium (2194) → Ħ'Attard → Mosta → Burmarrad → St Paul's Bay → Buġibba Moll (6193) → Buġibba Bay 1 (2527) TERMINUS. The return direction lists no Il-Qawra stop. Verify stop sides, safe walks and the onward hotel connection in the dated planner.
records.hours: Operator timetable read 11 October 2026 on a repeating 30-minute pattern. Toward Ta' Qali: Qawra 952 first 06:09–06:10, last 21:38–21:39; Ta' Qali Stadium 6227 first 06:34–06:43, last 22:03–22:08 depending on the variant, about 25–33 minutes after the Qawra times within the same run; Il-Qawra stops served roughly 06:08–21:39. RETURN: Stadium 2194 first 05:52, LAST LISTED 20:53; terminus Buġibba Bay 1 (2527) last listed 21:26–21:36 depending on the variant, about 33 minutes after Stadium 2194. The extracted page carries several timetable variants without reliable day-type context, so treat these as static-grid spans rather than trip-day guarantees and confirm the date-specific departure in the operator's planner.
records.description: Route 186 runs between Rabat and Buġibba and is the only route in the operator's tables that links Qawra's seafront stops directly to the Ta' Qali stadium stop, but it is ASYMMETRIC and that is the single most important transport fact for this trip. Traced stop by stop on 11 October 2026, the direction that serves Il-Qawra (Arznell 950, Luzzu 951, Qawra 952) runs toward Ta' Qali and Rabat, while the return from opposite-side Stadium stop 2194 lists NO Il-Qawra stop at all and terminates at Buġibba Bay 1 (2527). A return to AX ODYCY on Route 186 therefore always means alighting in the Buġibba area and boarding a second service toward Qawra, and the last listed return departure from Stadium 2194 is 20:53 — the binding constraint for a late playoff finish. One single fare covers both legs because onboard tickets are valid two hours with free transfers. These are published static departure grids for the current timetable, not a saved date-specific journey; the walk from stop 6227 or 2194 to the actual MFCC/BLAST gate has not been measured, and the onward Buġibba → Qawra connection must come from the dated planner rather than be inferred from the operator's stop lists.
records.notes: Operator route page with the stop-by-stop grids, read 11 October 2026: https://www.publictransport.com.mt/route/186/ . Stops confirmed in that page’s lists: Il-Qawra Arznell 950, Luzzu 951, Qawra 952, Ta’ Qali Gibjun 6118, Venture 6226, Stadium 6227 and Villagg 6228; Rabat 4 (2567) is the other terminus. The same page shows stops 6227/6228/2191 also served by Routes 56 and 202, and the Stadium 6227 stop is also listed for the Ta’ Qali Park & Ride shuttles 403, 404 and 405 — useful alternates to compare in the planner. Route 214 lists Qawra and Qali-area stops as a second option: https://www.publictransport.com.mt/route/214/ . For the Saturday 17 October evening diversion see the separate diversion record. Date-specific planner (not run here): https://www.publictransport.com.mt/journey-planner/ . The operator’s public notice of the 17 October diversion is at https://www.publictransport.com.mt/latest-service-updates/ . Second-session caveats (11 October 2026): the static page shows multiple time variants and earlier tighter bounds were withdrawn rather than presented as trip-day times; the date-specific planner is https://www.publictransport.com.mt/journey-planner/ . Return stop 2194 was independently re-read on 11 October; outbound 6227 and return 2194 are different direction stops, so no single clock range is asserted. Route 186 is a day route, so a single journey costs the day-route price and is covered by the 7-day Explore Adult card; the closest listed sales office to Qawra is the Buġibba Terminal: https://www.publictransport.com.mt/office-and-ticket-machine/ . Third-pass additions (11 October 2026): the full return chain toward Buġibba was traced stop by stop and contains no Il-Qawra stop — Rabat 2 (2569), Mdina (135), Saqqajja (4627), Qanpiena (2232), Telgha (2231), Snajja (2192), Villagg (2193), Stadium (2194), Venture (6134), Gibjun (4125), Ħ'Attard Sedqa (2457), Marg (2458), Gheneb (5674), Mosta Waqqafa (2196), Trincetta (2200), Gholja 2 (1101), Mithna (1099), Milt (1097), Gatt (1143), Kungress (1142), Rotunda 2 (2563), Isouard (1105), Kostituzzjoni (1106), Targa (1107), Gharusa (1200), Rihana (1202), Campra (1203), Ramez (1204), Burmarrad (1205), Qannotta (1206), Qadi (1207), Mwiezeb (956), Imhasel (958), Toni (6013), Gillieru (6014), Moll (6193), Rizzi (946), Sajf (947), Gzejjer (948), Buġibba Bay 1 (2527). Buġibba Bay 1 arrival is read as 21:26 in one variant and 21:36 in another on the same page, and a single 21:27 figure also appears in this dataset's event-day record; the variants are not labelled, so a range is reported and NO single clock time should be asserted. The mandatory onward transfer is recorded separately as route-186-return-transfer-bugibba. Two-hour transfer validity: https://www.publictransport.com.mt/fares-and-tickets/ . Two independent corroborations added by a parallel session and folded in here: BLAST's own attendee guide names “Malta Fairs & Conventions Centre – BLAST Arena Studios” at “Ta Qali, ATD 4000 Ħ’Attard”, which resolves the traveller-supplied “Attard” and the Ta’ Qali references as the SAME venue (see `blast-arena-studios-venue-address`), so routing to the Ta’ Qali Stadium stops is correct; and MFCC's own venue booklet states “BY BUS - FROM VALLETTA no.56, FROM SLIEMA no.202, FROM BUGIBBA no.186” (see `mfcc-official-bus-186`), making Route 186 venue-endorsed from the Buġibba/Qawra side as well as operator-listed. records.name: Route 186 diversion and the wider Ta’ Qali / Mosta evening detour cluster — 17–18 October, with two conflicting published windows
records.address: Route 186 toward Buġibba; affected stops listed by MPT are Gholja 2 through Targa
records.hours: Operator notices for the same diversion display two different evening windows: the Route 186 page reads weekly Friday/Saturday 19:00–00:00 starting 17 October (ending 18 October approx. 00:00), and the service-updates page read later on 11 October reads 20:00–24:00 for the same dated notice. Plan for the union, 19:00–24:00, and treat the live planner as authoritative.
records.description: Malta Public Transport carries a Route 186 detour notice for Friday/Saturday evenings starting 17 October 2026 and ending 18 October at approximately 00:00, stating that toward Buġibba the stops from Gholja 2 through Targa will not be served. The operator publishes TWO DIFFERENT evening windows for that same dated notice, and both were read on 11 October 2026: the Route 186 page shows it as 19:00–00:00, while the latest-service-updates page showed 20:00–24:00. Plan for the UNION, 19:00–24:00, and treat the live planner as authoritative on the day. Because 17 October is a Playoffs day and the notice names only those intermediate stops, it does not by itself say whether a Ta’ Qali Stadium departure or a Qawra-ward connection is cancelled — but the omitted segment is precisely the stretch between Ta’ Qali and Buġibba that the last listed 20:53 return uses, so a post-event bus return that evening may not run as the static grid shows. The same service-updates page lists a CLUSTER of further companion detours on the identical Friday/Saturday evening pattern from 17 October affecting Routes 31, 41, 42, 45, 47, 48, 103, 202, 203, 238, 260, 280, 405 and N48 in the Mosta, Rotunda and Ta’ Qali P&R area — including Route 405 omitting Rotunda 1 and Bezzina toward Mosta/Ta’ Qali P&R and Route 47 omitting Gatt through Rotunda 1 toward Mosta — so any Mosta-changing return plan needs rechecking too. A large open-air event is ticketed at UNO Malta in Ta’ Qali, Attard from 22:00 on Saturday 17 October, which is consistent with that cluster, but MPT names no cause and none is asserted here. The page also carries a separate, longer-running weekly Friday/Saturday 20:00–00:00 detour ending 21 April with the same affected-stop wording, so the operator is publishing overlapping notices. One ambiguity is worth flagging: 17 October 2026 is a Saturday and the notice’s explicit end is 18 October at approximately 00:00 (midnight ending Saturday), yet the same sentence says the detour runs “weekly on Friday, Saturday”, so whether it also applies on Friday 16 October is not clear from the text and must be checked with the operator or the planner. Treat the whole Ta’ Qali bus corridor as unreliable after 19:00 on 17 October and plan a taxi or ride-hailing return.
records.notes: Read 11 October 2026 on https://www.publictransport.com.mt/route/186/ under “Latest Service Updates”: a detour weekly on Friday and Saturday 19:00–00:00 starting 17 October, ending 18 October at about 00:00, “Toward Bugibba, stops from Gholja 2 through Targa will not be served”; and a second notice weekly on Friday and Saturday 20:00–00:00 ending 21 April with identical affected-stop wording. The same page also lists a stop closure at Saqqajja (ID 4627) on Routes 109, 109A, 181, 182, 186, 201, 202, 50, 51, 52, 53, 56 and N52, ends 1 January approximately 04:00, and Tuesday 13 October 09:30–17:30 construction detours on Attard Routes 54 and 106. All-service-updates page: https://www.publictransport.com.mt/latest-service-updates/ . Do not infer a cancelled or extra TWC service from these notices. The notice specifies affected stops rather than a total cancellation of Route 186, and it does not itself confirm whether a particular post-event bus will serve the required Qawra stop. Also listed on the operator’s service-updates page on 11 October 2026: Tuesday 13 October (09:30–17:30) construction detours on Attard Routes 54 and 106. Recheck the operator’s updates and planner on the day. Third-pass addition (11 October 2026), read on https://www.publictransport.com.mt/latest-service-updates/ : the wider Friday/Saturday 19:00–00:00 cluster from 17 October covers Routes 31, 41, 42, 45, 47, 48, 103, 202, 203, 238, 260, 280, 405 and N48 around Mosta, Rotunda and Ta' Qali P&R. MPT states no cause for the cluster; the UNO Malta event is recorded separately in data/activities.json from the official ticketing platform and is NOT presented as the operator's stated reason. The Route 186 notice wording is: "Detour in effect weekly on Friday, Saturday from 7:00 PM to 12:00 AM, starting October 17. Detour ends October 18 at approximately 12:00 AM. Toward Bugibba, stops from Gholja 2 through Targa will not be served." Independently re-read 11 October 2026 on https://www.publictransport.com.mt/latest-service-updates/ . The live notice reads: “Buses on Route 186 will be on detour. Detour in effect weekly on Friday, Saturday from 7:00 PM to 12:00 AM, starting October 17. Detour ends October 18 at approximately 12:00 AM. Toward Bugibba, stops from Gholja 2 through Targa will not be served.” Ambiguity to note: 17 October 2026 is a Saturday and the explicit end time is 18 October at approximately 12:00 AM (that is, midnight ending Saturday 17 October), yet the same sentence says the detour runs “weekly on Friday, Saturday”. Whether it also applies on Friday 16 October is therefore not clear from the text and must be checked with the operator or the planner. The notice also describes the Buġibba-bound direction only; it does not say whether the Ta’ Qali Stadium stops used by this trip are affected. A parallel re-read of the same pages on 11 October 2026 independently recorded the window discrepancy described above (19:00–00:00 on the Route 186 page against 20:00–24:00 on the service-updates page for the same dated notice) and judged the companion Mosta/Rotunda cluster to run 19:00–24:00; that reading is folded in here rather than kept as a second record. Neither reading resolves which window the operator will actually apply, so the union is used and the live planner remains authoritative.

records.hours: MPT’s Route TD1 timetable (read 11 Oct 2026) lists hourly departures from Airport 1 (stop 2550) on the hour from 05:00 to 00:00, reaching Il-Qawra stop Arznell (950) at 05:42–00:35; return departures toward Airport 3 (stop 2552) serve Il-Qawra stop Arznell (950) hourly at 05:28–23:26 on weekdays and 05:27–23:27 on weekends.
records.description: This is the most straightforward published public-bus option from Malta International Airport toward Qawra: Airport Direct TD1 runs from the airport toward Ċirkewwa via Buġibba and the Qawra area, and its operator timetable confirms service at Il-Qawra stop Arznell (ID 950) in both directions. The airport terminal is signposted from arrivals. Buses have luggage space; no advance booking is required. The precise walk from stop Arznell 950 to AX ODYCY was not independently measured.
records.notes: Route stop and times: https://www.publictransport.com.mt/route/TD1/. MPT also lists TD5 Airport Direct toward Rabat/Buġibba hourly at €3; its Qawra suitability was not established here. Operator information and fares: https://www.publictransport.com.mt/fares-and-tickets/. Independently re-read 11 October (chunks 7–9): both the Airport 1 outbound sequence (05:42–00:35 at Arznell 950) and the Ċirkewwa-to-Airport 3 return sequence (05:28–23:26 weekday / 05:27–23:27 weekend at Arznell 950) serve Il-Qawra stop Arznell 950. This supports route-level Qawra service in both directions, while the hotel walk and flight-specific departure still require a journey-planner check. Fare context re-verified 11 October 2026 against the operator’s own table, which lists Tallinja Direct routes at €3.00 and TD1 at €3.50: https://www.publictransport.com.mt/fares-and-tickets/ . The same page states that the 7-day Explore Adult card excludes tallinja Direct routes, while the 12 Single Day Journeys card may be used on the Airport Direct service at a cost of two journeys per trip.

records.address: Tickets may be purchased onboard by cash or contactless; sales points and machines are listed by MPT
records.hours: Tickets are valid for two hours with free transfers inside that window. Missed-ticket penalty: €50. Explore Child 7-day is €7.00 (ages 4–10). Cards and singles are sold at the airport, the Valletta and Buġibba terminals and Sliema Ferries, and the page does not print the 2026/27 winter changeover date.
records.description: The operator’s fare page, read 11 October 2026, publishes a single ticket table and a separate card table. Singles bought from the driver with cash, a contactless bank card or a phone are €2.00 (winter) or €2.50 (summer) on day routes and are valid for two hours with free transfers. The 12 Single Day Journeys card costs €19.00 and is shareable between travellers; the Explore Flex card costs €21.00 for four days or €27.00 for seven days and its offer grid explicitly includes Day Routes, Night Routes, Airport Direct and Special Services; the separate Explore Adult 7-day card at €25.00 explicitly excludes tallinja Direct Routes. A €50 penalty applies to travellers who cannot show a valid ticket, and cards must be validated on boarding. The page states the winter €2.00 single-fare period as running from 19 October 2025 to 13 June 2026, which does not resolve which single fare applies during 13–19 October 2026.
records.notes: Fare page read 11 October 2026: https://www.publictransport.com.mt/fares-and-tickets/ . Card-sales locations and machines: https://www.publictransport.com.mt/office-and-ticket-machine/ . TD1 Airport Direct detail: https://www.publictransport.com.mt/other-services/airport-direct/ . Worked comparison for a seven-day trip that includes airport days and daily event travel: Explore Flex 7-day €27.00 already includes Airport Direct, which would otherwise cost TD1 singles at €3.50 each way (€7.00 return); Explore Adult 7-day €25.00 plus two TD1 singles is about €32.00, and a 12-journey €19.00 card would be partly consumed by the two extra Airport Direct journeys. That comparison is arithmetic on published prices, not a quote, and assumes the traveller actually needs Airport Direct and daily buses. The page also sells Explore Flex bundle upgrades that add a Gozo Highspeed return (€42.00 for 7 days) or a harbour cruise (€42.00 for 7 days). Confirm activation, expiry and inclusions at a sales office before buying. Sales offices and ticket machines: https://www.publictransport.com.mt/office-and-ticket-machine/ . The page states that the €2.00 winter fare applied from 19 October 2025 to 13 June 2026 and lists a separate summer day-route fare of €2.50, but it does not print the 2026/27 winter start date, so the exact seasonal boundary for this trip stays open. Recheck the day before travel, because seasonal prices and card inclusions change. Re-read additions from a parallel session on 11 October 2026, folded in: Re-read additions 11 October: the Explore Flex card can also buy two Airport Direct trips for €6; sightseeing bundles are listed at €36/€42 (Gozo Highspeed return or Harbour Cruise, 4/7-day), €53/€59 (2 Islands), €68/€74 (2 Islands + cruise), €53/€59 (Golden Comino Escape, summer only) and €41/€51 (Hop-On Hop-Off); the shareable 12-journey card expires six months after first use and charges Airport Direct/Night at two journeys per trip. Explore Adult versus €27 Explore Flex comparison when Airport Direct is wanted, is worked out in the separate record trip-fare-scenarios-13-19-oct; the seasonal question is handled in mpt-seasonal-fare-window-2026 and sales points in mpt-card-sales-points.

records.name: Bus cost scenarios for this exact trip (13–19 October, seven days)
records.area: Malta and Gozo — one traveller, seven-day window
records.address: Not applicable — arithmetic on published MPT prices
records.hours: Prices as published on the MPT fares page on 11 October 2026; they can change.
records.description: Arithmetic only, so the choice can be made in seconds once the real number of rides is known. At the conservative €2.50 single fare, break-even against the €19 12-journey card is 8 journeys (7 × €2.50 = €17.50; 8 × €2.50 = €20.00), and against the €25 Explore Adult 7-day card it is 10 journeys. At €2.00 the 12-journey card breaks even at 10 journeys and the €25 card at 13. A realistic event week — airport transfer, several Qawra or Valletta leisure trips, and four or five event-day round trips — will exceed 10 single journeys for most travellers, so an unlimited seven-day card is the likely better value, while the €19 shareable 12-journey card suits a couple taking only a few trips together. One caveat changes the answer: TD1 Airport Direct is €3.50 per single and is excluded from the €25 Explore Adult card according to that card's own paragraph, whereas the €27 Explore Flex 7-day explicitly includes Airport Direct. If you intend to use the airport bus, compare the €27 Flex. Which single fare actually applies in October is handled in the separate seasonal-window record, which reasons that on the operator's own published pattern the cheaper winter single begins after 19 October, making €2.50 the planning figure for this trip; that is a planning inference, not a published trip-week fare. None of this is a quote, a reservation, or a prediction of how often you will actually ride.
records.notes: Every price used here was read directly from https://www.publictransport.com.mt/fares-and-tickets/ on 11 October 2026. The break-even figures are plain division of those published prices and assume each boarding is one journey; a two-leg return inside two hours counts as one fare because transfers are free. The October single-fare season is NOT established by the operator's page (its only dated winter window, 19 October 2025 – 13 June 2026, has expired), so both the €2.00 and €2.50 scenarios are shown. Card inclusions differ and are quoted from that page: Explore Flex unlimited offers include day routes, night routes, Airport Direct and special services; the Explore Adult 7-day paragraph excludes tallinja Direct routes. Confirm inclusions with MPT before buying. No traveller count, ride count, booking or reimbursement is assumed — enter your own figures in the expense planner. This record complements rather than repeats main-dataset records mpt-seasonal-fare-window-2026 (which fare applies), mpt-card-sales-points (where to buy) and mpt-fares-cards (the published table); it adds only the break-even arithmetic and the €25-versus-€27 Airport Direct comparison. records.name: BLAST Arena Studios Malta — “Attard” vs “Ta’ Qali” resolved
records.area: MFCC, Ta’ Qali — postal address Ħ’Attard ATD 4000
records.address: MFCC South Gate National Stadium, Millennium Stand, Attard ATD 4000, Malta (postal address). The complex sits in the Ta’ Qali national-park area between Attard, Rabat and Mosta; EventWorks notes the address is “only a postal address”.
records.hours: Not published for TWC. BLAST’s own fan guide for a separate 2026 event gives per-day venue door times (13:30 Thu, 13:00 Fri, 11:00 Sat, 10:30 Sun CEST) — do not transfer those to TWC.
records.description: Important disambiguation: the traveller-supplied “BLAST Arena Studios, Attard” and the Ta’ Qali references elsewhere in this guide are the SAME venue. BLAST’s own attendee guide names “Malta Fairs & Conventions Centre – BLAST Arena Studios” with the address “Ta Qali, ATD 4000 Ħ’Attard”, and the Malta Tourism Authority business directory lists it as “MFCC South Gate National Stadium, Millennium Stand, Attard ATD 4000”. Bus routing to the Ta’ Qali Stadium stops is therefore correct for this venue. What remains unconfirmed is the TWC-specific attendee pin, gate, entrance and daily door times.
records.notes: BLAST’s own attendee guide (https://blast.tv/cs/news/malta-fan-guide) states “Venue: Malta Fairs & Conventions Centre - BLAST Arena Studios / Address: Malta Fairs & Conventions Centre Ta Qali, ATD 4000 Ħ’Attard” and lists per-day door times for that separate 30 July–2 August 2026 event. Corroborated by EventWorks ticketing (https://eventworks.mt/slam-8): “BLAST Arena Studios Malta, MFCC South Gate National Stadium, Millennium Stand, Attard ATD 4000, Malta — Above address is only a postal address”; by GamingMalta (https://www.gamingmalta.org/event/blast-slam-viii/); and by the visitmalta.co.uk business directory. This resolves the place-name conflict for routing purposes only; it does NOT confirm TWC attendee access, entrance, ticket validity, daily schedule or event transport.
records.price range: Not applicable — venue identification, not a charge

records.name: MFCC’s own “getting here” guidance — Route 186 from Buġibba
records.address: MFCC venue booklet, “TA’ QALI / Ta’Qali National” getting-here section
records.hours: Not applicable — standing venue/operator guidance, not a timetable
records.description: Independent corroboration from the venue itself: the Malta Fairs & Conventions Centre’s own published venue booklet states “BY BUS - FROM VALLETTA no.56, FROM SLIEMA no.202, FROM BUGIBBA no.186”. Route 186 is therefore both the operator- and venue-endorsed bus from the Buġibba/Qawra side, which is the traveller’s base area. By car the booklet directs visitors from Valletta via Attard, passing Triq l-Imdina to the National Stadium.
records.notes: Primary venue-published PDF (pageAge 2021-05-26), so route numbers should be re-confirmed against the current MPT planner before travel. Corroborated by Moovit’s MFCC stop listing, which names “Stadium” and “Sriedek” as the nearest stops and routes 42, 51, 52, 54, 56, 186, 202 and 44 in the area (third-party, directory-grade). The MFCC booklet does not give a stop-to-entrance walking route, walking time or event-day frequency, and TWC has not published attendee transport instructions.
records.price range: Regular route fare; no event fare published by MFCC
